dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the wait probe match the pass's fetch shape (e.g. drop the status filter mismatch / reuse the reconciler's project-scoped JQL) or document why key-only is a sufficient proxy for the status-scoped fetch.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py:76: `return f'project = {_validate_project_key(project)} AND status = "Done" ORDER BY updated DESC'`

In practice a single Lucene index update makes the two query shapes equivalent once the created (non-Done) Task is indexed, so this is a mild soundness gap in the gate rather than a demonstrated failure.
dropped.finding:
The wait-until-searchable probe JQL does not match the JQL the reconcile pass actually issues, so a positive probe result does not strictly guarantee the pass's fetch will see the issue. The probe uses `project = "

" AND key = ""` (no status filter, quoted project), while the fetcher searches `project =

AND status != "Done"` and `project =

AND status = "Done"` (status-scoped, unquoted project).
scenarios: A Jira DC configuration where the created issue's default status is out of the active/Done windows, or where key-lookup and full-text status-filtered queries hit the index at different times, would let the probe pass while the pass still sees `inbound_differ total=0`.
